topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the scope of the lecture on cancer causation, and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Multifactorial causes and drivers of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental biology of cancer and examine the interplay between intrinsic genetic errors, hereditary risks, and environmental exposures across populations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental, chemical, and infectious carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how specific environmental, infectious, and chemical agents cause cancer through direct DNA damage, metabolic activation, promotional inflammation, and tissue-specific vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and prove their links to cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk assessment
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing key themes and framing environmental carcinogenic risk in the context of everyday risk-benefit decisions.
